literal: Love, shame, benevolence, compassion, along with truthfulness—[these] five [are] the pillars supporting nobility.
translation: Love, a sense of shame, benevolence, compassion, and truthfulness—these five are the pillars that support a noble character.
modern: அன்பு, பழி பாவங்களுக்கு நாணுதல், பிறருக்கு உதவுதல், இரக்கம் காட்டுதல், வாய்மை ஆகிய ஐந்து பண்புகளும் சான்றாண்மை என்னும் மாளிகையைத் தாங்கி நிற்கும் தூண்களாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the core components of perfect character (sāṉṟāṇmai) using the metaphor of a building supported by pillars. The poet lists five essential virtues: love towards all, a healthy sense of shame that prevents one from doing wrong, benevolence or social duty, compassion towards others, and truthfulness. These five qualities are described as the pillars (tūṇ) that firmly support (ūṉṟiya) the structure of nobility (cāl). Without any one of these pillars, the integrity of a person's character cannot be sustained.
